title: Coherent discrete quotient classes of a compact space are realized by a point
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a compact topological space, meaning that every open cover has a finite subcover. A discrete quotient $Q$ of $X$ means an equivalence relation on $X$ whose equivalence classes are open; write $|Q|$ for its set of classes and $\pi_Q:X\to |Q|$ for the quotient map. Write $A\preceq B$ when every $A$-class is contained in a $B$-class, and let $q_{AB}:|A|\to |B|$ send an $A$-class to its containing $B$-class. Suppose that for every discrete quotient $Q$ an element $z_Q\in |Q|$ is given and that $q_{AB}(z_A)=z_B$ whenever $A\preceq B$. Then there exists $x\in X$ such that $\pi_Q(x)=z_Q$ for every discrete quotient $Q$ of $X$. No Hausdorff, total disconnectedness, or nonemptiness hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.
